newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian state bank to launch Eurobonds.
newsitem.headline: Romanian state bank to launch Eurobonds.

text.p: State bank Banca Comerciala Romana SA (BCR) said it plans to launch Romania's first corporate bonds on the international capital markets through Merrill Lynch International.
"We want to continue along the way opened by the National Bank of Romania and place Romanian companies on the external capital markets," the bank said in a statement.
It did not give details of the Eurobond issue but they are expected to be clarified at a signing ceremony next Tuesday in Bucharest.

The BCR, which specialised in industry financing before the 1989 fall of communism, was reshaped in December 1990. It continue to manage the bulk of loans granted to industrial companies and its network is one of the strongest in Romania.
Its share capital was 109.1 billion lei at end-1995 when the bank's own funds amounted to 676.8 billion lei. Its assets top 4.7 trillion lei.
Merrill Lynch has handled two medium-term issues on capital markets for the National Bank -- a $50 million private placement last November and $225 million worth of three-year Eurobonds in June.
It is also arranging the first foreign issue by a Romanian city helping Bucharest city hall to raise up to $200 million from autumn municipal bonds to upgrade infrastructure.

Romania won its first credit ratings from major agencies in March. Japan Credit Rating agency awarded it a BB-plus score. somewhat higher than the BB- minus ratings of Standards and Poors and IBCA and BA-three from Moody's Investors Service. ($=3,177) -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
